_DURABLE_FINDINGS_2026-08-26.corrected_tactical_filter_passed_its_fir: UPDATED 2026-08-26T15:00Z -- THE OPEN QUESTION THIS KEY POSED HAS BEEN ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS NOT THE ENCOURAGING ONE. AS ORIGINALLY WRITTEN (13:52-14:05Z): the 2026-08-25 calibration work (local trailing-30-to-60-minute volume baseline + strict two-bar price clause + structural-level-only triggers) got its first LIVE candidate today and vetoed it with all three clauses failing independently -- magnitude 0.0014%, no hold on the following bar, 87.8% of the local baseline. That mattered because the 2026-08-25 audit could not distinguish discipline from a broken filter: four vetoes in a row look identical from the outside. The key then closed by naming the one test that would settle it -- 'the next thing to watch for is a candidate that CLEARS all three clauses, which is the only test that shows whether the corrected filter is selective or merely restrictive.' It has still never confirmed a trade. THAT CANDIDATE ARRIVED 20 MINUTES LATER AND THE FILTER CONFIRMED IT. At 14:25Z QQQ cleared every clause: a structural level (a 13:59Z tag of and rejection at the 20-day, 712.200 vs 712.1600), a completed 5-minute close under 710.00 (708.525) that HELD under on the following bar (708.946), on 247,350 against a 117,990 trailing-30-minute settled baseline = 209.6% -- half again the confirmation of the two 2026-08-25 fires (140%, 146%). AND IT RETRACED COMPLETELY INSIDE 30 MINUTES. Low 707.970, back to 710.309 and above the trigger line. So the filter is NOT merely restrictive -- it does confirm -- but its first confirmation was wrong, which makes this the FOURTH consecutive measured level-fire to fail (2026-08-25 15:30Z, 2026-08-25 17:00Z, and today's). WHAT THIS RULES OUT, which is the real value: the 2026-08-25 audit blamed the LEVEL -- self-drawn boxes get broken constantly -- and prescribed structural levels as the fix. Today's fire WAS on a structural level, correctly re-derived, on a feed reconciled against the 1-minute series, at higher confirmation volume, and it failed anyway. The level-quality hypothesis has now been tested and does not explain the failures. WHAT REPLACES IT: the confirming volume was IMPULSE, not PARTICIPATION. The bar after the fire collapsed to 68.7% of baseline and never recovered while price retraced 2.34 points. A 2.1x spike that dies in one bar is an air pocket into a session low, and on an event-eve tape that is the expected shape -- there is no participation available to extend ANY break when the whole market is waiting on one number due after the bell. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE FOR THE NEXT INSTANCE, stated as a hypothesis to test rather than a rule to obey: on an event-eve session treat a volume-confirmed structural break as NON-ACTIONABLE regardless of how clean it measures, and test the bar AFTER the fire for baseline persistence before crediting the fire at all. Verified on one fire only -- the 2026-08-25 following-bar volumes were never recorded, so this is not yet confirmed on them. Do not promote it to CLAUDE.md until a second fire tests it.

1_minute_feed_is_not_an_arbiter.promote_to: CLAUDE.md -- it CORRECTS an existing rule rather than adding one.
1_minute_feed_is_not_an_arbiter.claim_corrected: The feed rule set 2026-08-25T19:00Z prescribes reconciling aggregated bars against the 1-minute series because 'the 1-minute series is the arbiter and every coarser interval is a convenience.' MEASURED TODAY: the 1-minute series has the SAME defect. It is the best available series, not an arbiter.
1_minute_feed_is_not_an_arbiter.measurement: QQQ 2026-08-26T14:11Z, one bar, three fetches. At ~14:26Z: volume 10,006, OHLC 710.630 / 710.760 / 710.521 / 710.521. At ~14:29Z and again at ~14:31Z: volume 453, OHLC 710.545 / 710.570 / 710.545 / 710.560. A -95.5% volume revision with a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT OHLC, on a bar closed for fifteen minutes. Both cannot be right, and the later 453-share, 0.025-point-range bar wedged between neighbours of 20,981 and 29,138 carries the exact single-tick signature the original rule teaches you to spot in coarser intervals. Smaller same-window revisions on 13:46, 13:57, 14:13, 14:22 and 14:23 simultaneously.
1_minute_feed_is_not_an_arbiter.honest_size: It moved the candidate bucket from 104.4% to 105.7% of its trailing-30 mean -- above the line on both, so it changed NO decision today, which is exactly why it is safe to trust as a measurement. On a borderline reading it flips the answer, and the direction is unpredictable: revisions went both up and down inside one window.
1_minute_feed_is_not_an_arbiter.detector: Either defence suffices. (a) Fetch the window TWICE a few minutes apart and compare before a volume clause decides; disagreement means provisional, not quiet. (b) End the trailing baseline ~10 minutes back from now rather than at the last printed bar, so the clause is computed only on settled bars. Recognition rule generalises down one level: a 1-MINUTE bar whose volume is a tiny fraction of BOTH neighbours is provisional, not a quiet minute.
1_minute_feed_is_not_an_arbiter.lesson: The 2026-08-25 rule correctly refused to trust an interval merely for being fine-grained, then made the finest available interval the arbiter anyway. There is no arbiter in a live feed -- only settled data and a reconciliation. Trust the agreement between two reads, not the granularity of one.
1_minute_feed_is_not_an_arbiter.fourth_read_2026-08-26T15:16Z: THE DISAGREEMENT SETTLED, AND IT SETTLED ON THE LATER READ. A fourth pull of the same QQQ 14:11Z bar at 15:16Z -- 65 minutes after that bar closed, 45 minutes after the reads that produced this finding -- returns volume 453 and OHLC 710.545 / 710.570 / 710.545 / 710.560, identical to the 14:29Z and 14:31Z reads and still nothing like the 14:26Z read's 10,006 / 710.630-710.521. Three consecutive reads spanning 45 minutes now agree, and the outlier was the EARLIEST one. That is direct support for detector (a) as written -- trust the AGREEMENT between two reads, not the granularity of one -- and it adds the ordering this finding could not yet state: when an early read and a later read disagree, the later one is the one that persists. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, and no run should over-read it: 453 shares in a minute wedged between neighbours of 20,981 and 29,138, with a 0.025-point range, still carries the exact provisional signature this finding teaches you to distrust. Agreement across reads establishes only that the feed has STOPPED REVISING the bar; it does not establish that the bar is a true picture of that minute. Keep it out of any baseline denominator either way -- which today's 14:35Z-15:00Z window does by construction.

_DURABLE_FINDINGS_2026-08-26.a_stale_level_is_biased_toward_the_permi: COMPLEMENTS the sibling's retired_and_replaced correction, which found the same stale number independently at 15:15Z. Their finding is that the number in the PROSE was kept current while the number in the TRIGGER went stale. This adds the asymmetry and a detector, plus a retraction worth keeping. THE ASYMMETRY: a level written from the wrong window is not randomly wrong -- tape moves toward the levels that get written about, so the stale number tends to sit on the ALREADY-SATISFIED side. Measured: the stale 708.410 shrank the bearish clause's safety margin from 0.555 to 0.115, a ~5x reduction, entirely in the permissive direction. THE RETRACTION, which is the more useful half: this run first claimed the stale level would have MANUFACTURED A SECOND FIRE, reasoning from the 14:26Z/14:27Z MINUTE bars closing below it. That was wrong -- the clause is a completed 5-MINUTE close, and the 14:25Z 5-minute bar closed 708.525, above both versions. Neither fired. The error is instructive because it is this file's own recurring shape pointed at itself: a claim about a trigger was tested against the WRONG BAR INTERVAL, which is the same category as testing it against the wrong window or the wrong board. WHEN AUDITING A CLAUSE, TEST IT AT THE EXACT GRANULARITY THE CLAUSE SPECIFIES -- a minute bar is not evidence about a 5-minute clause. DETECTOR for the underlying bug: a level quoted as 'the session low/high' must be recomputed as min()/max() over the session's bars at the moment it is USED, never carried forward as a literal.
_DURABLE_FINDINGS_2026-08-26.tactical_arming_rationale_corrected: The 15:00Z retirement note says 'NEITHER IS ARMED INTO TONIGHT'S PRINT -- a hold spanning the NVDA report is not a scalp.' THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES ANYWAY, on a better ground that is same-day and measured: the fully-corrected filter fired this morning at 209.6% of baseline -- the strongest confirmation this desk has recorded -- and the move was void inside 30 minutes, with the bar after the fire collapsing to 68.7%. Level breaks are not being followed in this tape, which is what a market waiting on one number after the bell looks like. So the levels stay armable and the bar for acting on a fire is RAISED to include the proposed persistence clause, not lowered. Recorded so no run inherits a correct conclusion resting on a reason that does not hold -- a check that passes for the wrong reason is this desk's most-repeated defect.
_DURABLE_FINDINGS_2026-08-26.the_first_large_UPWARD_1_minute_revision:
MEASURED 2026-08-26T15:32Z, and it completes today's 14:31Z finding from the opposite direction. That earlier run proved 1-minute bars are revised after they close (a -95.5% volume revision with a changed OHLC) and noted revisions 'ran both up and down' without having measured a large up-side case. Here it is: QQQ's 15:29Z bar, read twice ONE MINUTE APART, went from volume 1,756 / open 710.450 / high 710.450 / close 710.400 to volume 12,835 / open 710.590 / high 710.660 / close 710.470 -- a +630.9% volume revision with a different OHLC. It carries the exact signature the rule teaches: a bar whose volume is a tiny fraction of BOTH neighbours (7,968 and 22,840) is PROVISIONAL, not a quiet minute. Three other bars in the same window revised materially (15:14 -13.9%, 15:18 +10.7%, 15:26 -4.7%), so this is a live property of the feed, not a one-off.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE NEW LESSON, AND IT IS A HOLE IN THE EXISTING FIX. The 'end the trailing baseline ~10 minutes back' rule protects the DENOMINATOR and nothing else. A provisional bar in the last minutes of the CANDIDATE window sits inside the numerator and outside a baseline that already ended ten minutes ago, so its revision is ONE-SIDED by construction. Measured exactly here: the revision moved the candidate 5-minute bar +28.6% (37,572 -> 48,331) while moving the baseline -0.11% (94,849 -> 94,749), lifting the confirmation reading from 39.7% to 51.0% of baseline. That is the FALSE-POSITIVE direction -- the same dangerous direction as the dropped-bucket defect, arriving through the opposite mechanism.

THE FIX, symmetric with the one already in the playbook: the final bar of a candidate window is the single bar most likely to be provisional AND the one whose revision cannot be offset. So either end the CANDIDATE window ~10 minutes back as well, or double-read its constituent minutes before letting it confirm. This run did the latter -- two fetches a minute apart, merged, disagreements resolved to the later read.

HONEST SCOPE, and it is what makes the audit credible: this changed NO decision today. The price clause failed outright, and 51% of baseline still fails the volume clause decisively. A filter's inputs can only be audited honestly on a day the correction does not flip the answer -- and the uncorrected 39.7% would have supported a stronger 'volume has collapsed' claim than the data actually carries, which is the small dishonesty this catch prevents.
_DURABLE_FINDINGS_2026-08-26.pre_event_volume_vacuum_is_a_measurable_: Participation halving in thirty minutes on a flat index (94,749 -> 48,331 per 5-minute bar, monotonic over four bars) is a measurement, and it makes a specific forward prediction rather than a vibe: any level break arriving in this state cannot clear a volume-confirmation clause calibrated on a live baseline, so the tactical track is effectively closed until participation returns. State that as the reason for standing down, rather than reporting 'no trigger' as though the tape were merely quiet -- the two look identical from the outside and only one of them tells the next instance what to watch for.
_DURABLE_FINDINGS_2026-08-26.a_trigger_keyed_to_the_prior_day_close_s: Worth recording before a future run treats today's near-misses as meaningful. QQQ's completed 5-minute closes crossed the 710.72 prior-day close FOUR times before 14:10Z (below at 13:30/13:35, above 13:40, below 13:45, above 13:50-14:05, below since), and price has spent the last fourteen bars inside 709.09-710.71, i.e. hugging just under it. A 'close above the prior close' clause on such a day fires on the morning drift and then goes silent while price oscillates a penny beneath it -- it is measuring the tape's noise amplitude, not a decision. The prior close IS a structural level, which is why it was correctly chosen over a desk-drawn box; the point is narrower and still real: STRUCTURAL IS NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT. A structural level that today's price has already closed on both sides of several times has no remaining information in it, and the 0.010 near-miss at 15:05Z should be read as chop touching a magnet, not as a setup one tick from triggering.

volume_clause_denominator_collapse.title: A TRAILING-LOCAL VOLUME BASELINE INVERTS IN A DECAYING TAPE: THE CLAUSE GETS EASIER EXACTLY WHERE IT SHOULD GET HARDER. Measured 2026-08-26T15:52Z on the session's first clean bullish fire.
volume_clause_denominator_collapse.measurement: QQQ 15:40-15:44Z candidate bucket = 98,957 shares (read B; read A 100,833, agreeing within 1.9%). Against the settled trailing-30-ending-10-back baseline of 66,144 it reads 149.6% and CONFIRMS. Against the same session's own earlier baselines it reads 80.1% (13:45-14:14, 123,470), 84.8% (14:05-14:34, 116,660), 83.9% (the 117,990 that today's 15:00Z fire cleared at 209.6%) and 39.8% of the actual 14:25Z flush bucket (248,511). The same absolute volume fails the clause at 13:45Z and passes it at 15:40Z, on a tape where participation fell rather than rose.
volume_clause_denominator_collapse.mechanism: The 2026-08-25 calibration rule correctly replaced a session-average denominator with a trailing-local one, because the opening hour's 254,448/bar made midday fires impossible. That fix is right and stays. What nobody checked is the other end: a trailing-local mean tracks a DECAYING tape downward, so as participation drains the bar to clear falls with it. In a pre-event vacuum the clause stops asking 'did participation arrive' and starts asking 'is this bar busier than the vacuum' -- which any drift back toward normal satisfies. The filter is self-fulfilling exactly when the tape is least informative.
volume_clause_denominator_collapse.why_it_survived: Both denominator defects are invisible from outcomes and point in OPPOSITE directions, so neither is detectable by counting fires. A session-average baseline vetoes everything and looks like discipline; a collapsed local baseline confirms everything and looks like the filter finally working. The 15:30Z run predicted a clean fire would FAIL on volume and treated a volume-confirmed break as 'far more informative than usual' -- exactly backwards, and it was refuted fifteen minutes later. A run that inherits that framing reads a vacuum fire as high-conviction.
volume_clause_denominator_collapse.detector: Report the candidate bar's volume in ABSOLUTE terms alongside the ratio, and test it against the session's OWN earlier baselines as well as the trailing-30 mean. Confirmation requires BOTH: at or above the trailing local mean AND not materially below the session's established bucket rate. A bar that clears the local baseline while sitting under the session's own typical bucket is baseline collapse, not participation -- decline it and say which of the two it was.
volume_clause_denominator_collapse.honest_scope: This changed no decision on the day it was found: the fire was declined on five independent merits (magnitude 0.044%, a mid-range level, both MAs overhead and untouched, ex-gap IV/RV 1.1697, no catalyst), and the follow-through reverted to 103% of baseline with price flat, so the trade was bad on the tape as well as on the filter. That is the only condition under which a filter's inputs can be audited credibly -- the same standard the 2026-08-25 calibration finding set for itself.
volume_clause_denominator_collapse.class: Same family as every denominator finding in CLAUDE.md: a constant or a window encoded an assumption about a moving thing, nothing errored, and the wrong behaviour was indistinguishable from the right one. Here the assumption was that a locally-calibrated baseline is always the conservative choice. It is not; it is conservative in a rising tape and permissive in a draining one.

count_the_crossings_before_trading_a_bre.finding: COUNT HOW MANY TIMES PRICE HAS CROSSED A LEVEL THIS SESSION BEFORE TRADING A BREAK OF IT. 'STRUCTURAL BY TYPE' IS NOT 'STRUCTURAL IN BEHAVIOUR'.
count_the_crossings_before_trading_a_bre.the_gap_it_closes: The 2026-08-25 rule lists the ACCEPTABLE CATEGORIES of level (moving average, session high/low, prior-day close, gap edge, prior swing) to stop the desk drawing its own boxes. A category test is not self-enforcing: today's prior-day close 710.72 passes it cleanly and is still the wrong level, because price crossed it ~6 times in one session and it lives in the middle of the range. A desk that has picked a level off the approved list believes it has complied -- the same shape as the 2026-08-25 finding that a desk which has computed ONE moving average believes it has complied.
count_the_crossings_before_trading_a_bre.the_detector: Before trading a break, count the session's crossings of the level. More than ~2 and it is functioning as a PIVOT, not a boundary -- decline regardless of how clean the volume looks. Then state where the level sits inside the day's range: a level in the interior cannot be a break, only an oscillation. Both are free from bars already fetched.

The IV method deliberately reads the expiry nearest 30 DTE; that is correct for its purpose and must not be changed. But a 30-DTE board spanning an event blends event premium with ordinary positioning and dilutes the event across a much longer window, so its level is a poor proxy for what the market expects the event ITSELF to do. Measured on NVDA hours before its print: the 2026-08-28 210 straddle (the first expiry after the event) priced an implied move of +/-5.806% (12.20 on 210.135 spot) versus +/-5.975% from the prior session's settled closes (12.73 on 213.05) -- CONTRACTING -- while the 30-DTE board rose 0.4108 -> 0.4144 and every run that day called it 'event premium peaking into the print'. DETECTOR, and it is two quotes: for any name with a known event inside the hold window, quote the ATM straddle on the FIRST expiry after the event and divide by spot; compare it to the SAME straddle's prior-session close. Rising = the event is being bid; flat or falling = expectations have stopped expanding regardless of what the 30-DTE row says. THE SHAPE, which is this file's most-repeated defect arriving through a new door: a correct measurement of the wrong board was allowed to answer a question it was never measuring, and nothing errored -- the conclusion was even right. An RSI2>=70 print on an underwater position is an OPTIONAL exit-into-strength and therefore requires the same discretionary judgment as any other loss-taking -- which under HARD RULE 5 means a HARD RULE 7 thesis break, not a technical trigger. THE TRANSFERABLE SHAPE, and it is this file's most-repeated one: a newly-granted authority arrives with wording compressed for brevity, and the first run to hold it is the run most likely to read the compression literally. When a new prompt's one-line summary of a rule is broader than the rule it summarizes, the RULE governs -- and the governance clause says so explicitly ('where either is stricter, the stricter rule applies').
